title: Python: PEP 695 type-parameter bounds and constraints are not walked
description: Record-only follow-up from GCLI-112's round 3 review (opum-ai/glyph-cli#220, landed 3a422ec1), accepted in DEC-303 (a72) item 3 as N4; ordinary, not on the hold list. CORRECTED under DEC-303 (a74) item 3 to what was run on origin/dev 4e186bfb: the bounds and constraints of a DEF (def h[T: C], def h[T: (A, B)]) and of a CLASS (class K[T: C]) are NOT walked: the walker pushes no children of that type_parameter, so a call or name read inside such a bound is never recorded as a call site or a class-body use (measured: def f[T: x.run()](self) and class K[T: x.run()] record only the x = C() call, no edge). The bounds of a type ALIAS ARE walked, because the alias case pushes its left side, type parameters included, in the enclosing scope; that case gives a wrong edge on dev and is tracked by its own hold task, GCLI-146. GCLI-112 only reads the declared names from the list (typeParameterNames); the typeParams null refusal in enumerableBindings is accepted as defensive with no fixture. Not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decide whether a call inside a bound or constraint (def h[T: f()]) is a call site, and in which scope it resolves (the type-parameter scope, lazily)
Fixtures red before and green after, measured against dev by running both; the five-pin delta (the corpus has no PEP 695) identical or reported
